requirement_title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement_text:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234
Type: bug

## Requirement

The analyzer does not work if `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

(The upstream issue contains no further text, repro or comments. Anything beyond this is derived.)

## Acceptance criteria

- With `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`, the MessagePack analyzer still reports its diagnostics (MsgPack0xx rules) for code that violates them. (derived)
- Behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` matches version 3.1.0, where the analyzer worked. (derived)
- Behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration` unset or false does not change. (derived)
- Source generation itself stays suppressed when `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue.

checked.what: Existing SourceGenerator tests on head: 175/175 passed, 0 failed
Existing SourceGenerator tests on base: 167/167 passed, 0 failed

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The README states MsgPack011, MsgPack016 and MsgPack017 are deliberately not reported for SuppressSourceGeneration types and the test asserts it. This matches the recorded decision, so it is not a defect.
Receipts/SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (2/3), passes on head (3/3); refutes 1 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-2
Receipts/SecurityDepthStepOffByOneTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 2/2 failed
Mutation: 6 killed, 9 survived, 0 compile errors, 0 timeouts (15 mutants on TypeCollector.cs, MessagePackSecurity.cs)

findings.claim: `DepthStep` changed from `>=` to `>`, an off-by-one that admits one more nesting level than `MaximumObjectGraphDepth`. With the default `UntrustedData` limit of 500, a 501-deep graph is now accepted. A configured limit of N now allows N+1 levels, and a limit of 0 now allows one level. This weakens the stack-depth protection described in L9. It is unrelated to REQ-2234 (analyzer behaviour with `SuppressSourceGeneration`), and the acceptance criteria require unrelated behaviour to stay unchanged.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.SecurityDepthStepOffByOneTests. With `MaximumObjectGraphDepth = 1` and `reader.Depth = 1`, `DepthStep` throws `InsufficientExecutionStackException` on base but not on head. With limit 0 and depth 0 it also throws on base only. (generated tests: DepthStep_ThrowsWhenDepthEqualsMaximum, DepthStep_ZeroMaximumRejectsAnyNesting)

findings.claim: The off-by-one change from `>=` to `>` in DepthStep alters the maximum allowed depth by one (a security-relevant limit). It is unrelated to the requirement and no test in the diff covers the boundary, so no test would fail if the mutation were reverted or made differently.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs:233 off-by-one: reader.Depth > this.MaximumObjectGraphDepth -> reader.Depth >= this.MaximumObjectGraphDepth; expected to survive because no test in the diff exercises depth boundary behaviour

findings.claim: All new duplicate-key tests use properties only. The second set of ContainsKey guards and the `continue` (around lines 1145-1180) is not exercised by any test with fields, so deleting those guards would survive.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1163 remove-guard: `if (!intMembers.ContainsKey(member.IntKey))` -> unconditional Add; expected to survive because every duplicate-key test declares properties, not fields

findings.claim: the change's tests do not detect delete-statement at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1165
the change's tests do not detect negate-condition at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1179
the change's tests do not detect remove-guard at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1179
the change's tests do not detect delete-statement at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1181

hunches.claim: The change edits `MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep` from `>=` to `>`. Nothing in REQ-2234 asks for this, and it is a security behaviour change. A graph nested exactly `MaximumObjectGraphDepth` levels deep used to throw `InsufficientExecutionStackException` and is now accepted, so the depth limit (500 by default) effectively becomes limit+1 for all users. The requirement is limited to the analyzer and `SuppressSourceGeneration`, and ledger L12 covers a different depth change.

receipt_plan.detail: Build a msgpack payload of nested arrays exactly `MessagePackSecurity.Default.MaximumObjectGraphDepth` levels deep. Deserialize it as `object` with `MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard`. Base throws `MessagePackSerializationException` (inner `InsufficientExecutionStackException`); head succeeds.

hunches.claim: Off-by-one change in DepthStep: `>=` became `>`, so the effective maximum nesting depth grows by one. Input nested exactly MaximumObjectGraphDepth+1 deep used to throw InsufficientExecutionStackException and now deserializes. This is a security-relevant behavior change on untrusted data, and it has nothing to do with the analyzer/SuppressSourceGeneration requirement. Users who set a small limit, or who rely on the documented 500 limit, will see different accept/reject behavior without opting in.

receipt_plan.detail: Set MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(N) (e.g. N=3). Deserialize an object[] nested N+1 levels deep, built with MessagePackWriter. On base it throws InsufficientExecutionStackException. On head it succeeds. Compare the outcome of base and head.

hunches.claim: The new `continue` on a key-kind mismatch changes generator output for types that mix int and string keys. Previously the mismatched member fell through and was added to the member dictionaries, and the formatter was generated with it. Now that member is dropped from the generated formatter, so the emitted code differs for users who check in or snapshot generator output. The MsgPack diagnostic is still reported, so the build already fails for these types, but the output change is still visible. This is only partly tied to the requirement, which asks for the analyzer to work under SuppressSourceGeneration.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator snapshot tests on a [MessagePackObject] type with one [Key(0)] member and one [Key("a")] member. Compare the generated formatter on base and head. Head omits the mismatched member.

hunches.claim: Duplicate [Key] values (int or string) are now silently deduplicated with ContainsKey, so the first member wins and the later one is dropped from the generated formatter. Base threw ArgumentException on the duplicate Add, which the generator or analyzer may have surfaced as a crash. If the duplicate-key diagnostic (MsgPack006) is reported elsewhere, this is safe. If it is not, a generated formatter can now silently lose a member, with no wire-format error. The diff does not show whether MsgPack006 is always reported before this point.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test on a [MessagePackObject] type with two members both marked [Key(0)]. Assert MsgPack006 is reported and that no exception is thrown. Also run the generator on the same type and check the generated Serialize for the dropped member.

hunches.claim: DepthStep changed the check from `reader.Depth >= MaximumObjectGraphDepth` to `>`. This allows one extra nesting level beyond the configured MaximumObjectGraphDepth, so the limit is off by one on every deserialization path, including UntrustedData. Nothing in the requirement (a SuppressSourceGeneration analyzer bug) or the ledger covers loosening this recursion/depth protection. L12 only concerns a 500 to 5000 change and says to follow the requirement, so it does not authorize this one.

receipt_plan.detail: Set MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(N). Deserialize a payload nested exactly N levels deep, so that reader.Depth equals N at the deepest DepthStep call. Base throws InsufficientExecutionStackException; head does not. Also run the existing MessagePackSecurity depth tests, which would fail if they assert the exact boundary.

hunches.claim: The MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep change from >= to > is unrelated to the requirement. It allows one extra level of depth and changes runtime security behavior, which could break the stack depth limit of 500 and existing depth tests.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing MessagePackSecurity / MaximumObjectGraphDepth tests, and serialize an object graph nested exactly MaximumObjectGraphDepth deep, comparing base and head. The head build should accept one more level than base.

hunches.claim: The diff does not show the change that stops the analyzer from skipping suppressed types. Only the TypeCollector duplicate-key guards are visible, so the core fix (analyzer reports diagnostics when SuppressSourceGeneration = true) may live in an unseen hunk. The tests cover MsgPack003/004/005/015 but do not cover MsgPack012.

receipt_plan.detail: Revert the suppression-skip fix and run the new analyzer tests. Also add a MsgPack012 case for a suppressed type, since the README claims it is reported.

hunches.claim: The `continue` added after the DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys diagnostic is only observed through the MsgPack005 markup test, and the mixed-keys test does not assert MsgPack00x mix diagnostics specifically; removing `continue` would still add a member to the wrong dictionary without a test failure, since the ContainsKey guard hides collisions. Only one of the two TypeCollector locations (the one reached via the property/field loop) is likely covered, and the test uses properties only, so the field-path duplicate (second hunk pair at ~1145-1180) is uncovered.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1008 remove-guard: delete `continue;`; expected to survive because MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure only asserts the reported diagnostic and the ContainsKey guards prevent any crash

hunches.claim: The suppressed-source-generation analyzer tests may pass on base: the source diff contains no change in how SuppressSourceGeneration is handled (the visible TypeCollector changes only guard duplicate keys). Tests MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported and MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported do not reproduce the reported bug in this diff and would likely pass on base too.

receipt_plan.detail: Run SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported and MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported against base-built analyzer; if they pass, they do not reproduce the bug

hunches.claim: No analyzer release note or doc change accompanies the behavioral change. The README says MsgPack003/004/005/012/015 are now reported for suppressed types, but the individual doc/analyzers pages are not updated. This is a minor docs convention gap.

receipt_plan.detail: Check doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md and MsgPack005.md for any mention of SuppressSourceGeneration.

hunches.claim: NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType is weak: GetFormatter returning null would also happen for any type absent from the resolver, and the roundtrip test passes via the dynamic resolver regardless of the analyzer fix. Neither ExecutionTest exercises the analyzer.

receipt_plan.detail: Execution tests assert runtime behaviour only; they would pass on base since they do not touch the analyzer path
